papers.title: One night of sleep deprivation reduces spatially patterned human brain clearance: implications for simulated tau propagation
papers.summary: Using Bayesian inference on CSF tracer-enhanced MRI in 21 subjects, the study estimated region-specific brain clearance rates that were spatially patterned and highest in entorhinal cortex, decreasing in Braak stage order. One night of sleep deprivation reduced mean clearance while preserving the spatial pattern, and computational simulations showed that clearance level sets tau propagation timescale while spatial pattern shapes accumulation and onset.

papers.title: Symptoms of anxiety are linked to N3 sleep and lower dissipation of slow-wave activity during nocturnal sleep.
papers.summary: In 70 healthy conscripts, elevated anxiety was associated with weaker dissipation of slow-wave activity (SWA) across NREM episodes and a greater proportion of N3 sleep, independent of depression. Higher anxiety also correlated with elevated alpha power during REM sleep, suggesting cortical hyperarousal.

papers.title: Inhibition of Cerebellar Dentate Nucleus-Zona Incerta Glutamatergic Circuit Improves Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model.
papers.summary: Using optogenetic and chemogenetic inhibition of the cerebellar dentate nucleus-zona incerta glutamatergic circuit in a pilocarpine mouse model of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy, the study found reduced sleep fragmentation, increased sleep duration, and improved sleep quality. The authors propose targeting this circuit as a therapeutic strategy for TLE-associated sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Enhanced local synchronization with impaired large-scale recruitment of NREM slow waves in pediatric disorders of arousal
papers.summary: Using 256-channel high-density EEG in 17 children with disorders of arousal and 17 matched controls, this study found that children with DOA showed larger, steeper, and more locally synchronized slow waves but reduced large-scale cortical recruitment, particularly for Type 1 slow waves. They also had reduced centro-posterior slow spindle density, indicating altered NREM oscillation coordination despite preserved conventional sleep architecture.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm maturation in infancy: a large-scale analysis of sleep-wake pattern development from 3 to 18 months based on longitudinal data.
papers.summary: A large-scale longitudinal analysis of sleep logs from 175,593 infants found that total sleep decreased from 14.8 h at 3 months to 12.5 h at 18 months, driven by reduced daytime sleep as nap frequency declined from 3.9 to 1.0 per day. Bedtime regularity increased most steeply before 9 months, and individual differences in bedtime regularity were highly stable across age periods.

papers.title: A brain circuit linking sleep loss to pain.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a study identifying a retrosplenial cortex–anterior cingulate cortex–zona incerta circuit that contributes to heightened mechanical and heat sensitivity after sleep deprivation in male mice, highlighting a specific brain pathway linking sleep loss to pain.

papers.title: Circadian timing does not modulate human temporal contrast sensitivity.
papers.summary: A 40-hour forced desynchrony protocol in 12 participants found decisive Bayesian evidence against circadian modulation of cone-mediated temporal contrast sensitivity at 2 Hz and 8 Hz for luminance and chromatic stimuli. The results suggest that previously reported time-of-day effects may reflect homeostatic or non-circadian factors.

papers.title: AMPK-dependent brain-wide norepinephrine release promotes recovery from metabolic coma in mice
papers.summary: In mouse models of metabolic coma, hypoglycemia triggered AMPK-dependent excitation of nucleus tractus solitarius neurons that activated locus coeruleus norepinephrine neurons via a glutamatergic circuit. This drove brain-wide norepinephrine release at ~10-fold higher magnitude than physiological sleep-wake release and promoted arousal, with vagus nerve stimulation accelerating recovery.

papers.title: Sleep-related Brain Activity in an Arousal-reducing Agent-induced Mouse Model Evaluated with fMRI.
papers.journal: Magnetic resonance in medical sciences : MRMS : an official journal of Japan Society of Magnetic Resonance in Medicine
papers.summary: Resting-state fMRI in mice compared functional connectivity under zolpidem, lemborexant, and dexmedetomidine, finding that zolpidem induced the smallest overall connectivity differences and dexmedetomidine the largest. Common sleep-like network reorganization was accompanied by agent-specific connectivity patterns.

papers.title: Investigating the transfer of physical stimuli to the dreamed body: A comparative study of muscular, vestibular, and haptic stimulation on dream incorporation.
papers.summary: In a within-subject sham-controlled study with 24 participants, electrical muscular, galvanic vestibular, and haptic vibration stimulation during REM sleep did not produce statistically significant modality-specific dream incorporation compared to sham. The findings highlight methodological challenges and suggest contextual or expectancy effects may contribute to bodily dream content.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Persistent Venous Narrowing of Downstream Parenchymal Microvessels and Pial Veins in the Male Mouse Cortex.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.summary: In male mice, 2-week chronic intermittent hypoxia (8% O2, 6.5-min cycles, 6 h/day) selectively reduced pial vein (55 to 46 μm) and parenchymal venule (9.9 to 8.2 μm) diameters, increased arterio-venous transit time, and impaired neurovascular coupling, while arteries and arterioles were unaffected. An endothelin receptor antagonist reversed these impairments except pial vein constriction.

papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Integration of Video and EEG Reveals Distinct Seizure Phenotypes in Mouse Models of Epilepsy.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: An integrated machine learning pipeline combining EEG and behavioral video data classified seizures in mice, outperforming unimodal EEG- or video-based approaches and matching experienced human scorers. It validated on a pharmacologically induced generalized seizure model and a genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy model, revealing distinct atypical behavioral and typical non-behavioral spike-wave discharge events.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.summary: In an exploratory secondary analysis of 26 MCI patients from a randomized sham-controlled trial, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) was associated with changes in parietal delta-band EEG power. Relative delta power changes at P1, P2, and P5 positively correlated with MoCA-B improvement, while absolute delta power changes negatively correlated with AVLTN7 improvement, though these correlations did not survive multiple comparison correction.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.summary: In 83 young adults, an experimental frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task increased midfrontal theta power following frustrative nonreward and during high-effort trials, while decreasing self-reported state motivation and increasing frustration, arousal, and response speed. Higher state frustration reduced response vigor during effort execution after unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: Chronotherapeutic and Circadian Rhythm-Based Strategies in Diabetes Management: A Critical Opinion Based on Evidences.
papers.summary: This critical review integrates chronobiological evidence to propose personalized chronotherapy for diabetes management, emphasizing circadian timing of meals, drugs, exercise, sleep, and light exposure. It concludes that circadian timing is a promising adjuvant but current evidence does not identify an optimal intervention time.

papers.title: In-laboratory polysomnography as the reference standard in sleep research: a bibliometric overview of human studies.
papers.summary: This bibliometric review analyzed 462 in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) studies from 2015–2025, showing steady publication growth led by the United States and China, with a stable thematic core of sleep monitoring, staging, and apnea, alongside emerging trends in machine learning, wearables, and brain modeling.

papers.title: Respiratory event duration reveals novel phenotypes beyond the apnea-hypopnea index in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: Using polysomnography data from 959 adults with obstructive sleep apnea, clustering that included longest apnea and hypopnea durations identified four phenotypes beyond AHI-based severity, including a prolonged-apnea phenotype with only moderate AHI and another with long event durations and pronounced nocturnal hypoxemia. Respiratory event duration provided complementary temporal characterization of OSA phenotypes.

papers.title: Night-to-night sleep variability and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective cohort study with a complementary in vitro circadian-disruption experiment.
papers.summary: In 7,604 NHANES adults followed for a median 81 months, greater night-to-night sleep variability (midpoint, onset, and total sleep time SDs) and lower sleep regularity index were associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Complementary HUVEC experiments showed that irregular dexamethasone schedules reduced core clock-gene expression, lowered Griess assay absorbance, and increased inflammatory and adhesion-marker expression compared with a regular schedule.

papers.title: Association of Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet with sleep quality and quantity, inflammation and oxidative stress in Iranian adults: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 535 Iranian adults, highest adherence to the MIND diet was associated with 54% lower odds of short sleep and 56% lower odds of poor sleep quality, with stronger associations in overweight/obese participants. No significant associations were found with inflammatory or oxidative stress biomarkers.

papers.title: Effectiveness of school-based sleep promotion programs for adolescents: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 34 studies (22,679 adolescents) evaluated school-based sleep promotion programs. Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found significant improvements in sleep knowledge (SMD=0.99), sleep hygiene (SMD=-0.20), and depressive symptoms (SMD=-0.70), but no significant effects on sleep quality, sleep efficiency, or total sleep time.

papers.title: Vortioxetine-Associated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep Alterations: A Focused Narrative Review of Human Polysomnographic Evidence.
papers.summary: This focused narrative review examines the relationship between vortioxetine and REM sleep, integrating sleep neurobiology, vortioxetine pharmacology, and limited human polysomnographic evidence from principally two studies. It concludes that vortioxetine-associated REM changes are best regarded as a pharmacodynamic effect whose persistence, dose dependence, mechanism, and clinical relevance remain uncertain, and have not been established as surrogate markers of antidepressant response or other meaningful outcomes.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.summary: This study recorded 19-channel EEG from 17 emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during rest and a standardized cognitive challenge to test whether chronic occupational cognitive demand alters EEG stress biomarkers. The challenge robustly produced frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta across groups, but no Group x Condition interaction survived correction, indicating an absence of detectable large group differences, with Bayesian analysis showing moderate evidence for the null for alpha and theta features.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Exploratory Pharmacodynamics of Melanin-Concentrating Hormone Receptor-1 Antagonist RGH-706 in Healthy and Overweight or Obese Men.
papers.summary: This Phase 1 program evaluated the novel melanin-concentrating hormone receptor-1 antagonist RGH-706 in healthy men (Study A) and overweight or obese men (Study B), showing dose-proportional pharmacokinetics up to 62.5 mg, a terminal half-life of 29-35 hours, and good tolerability. Exploratory pharmacodynamic measures showed trends toward lower total energy intake, preference for fatty foods, and weight gain, primarily at lower doses of 2.5 and 7.5 mg/day.

papers.title: Nonlinear associations between sleep duration and psychological frailty in an aging Chinese population: insights from a national cohort.
papers.summary: In 9,476 middle-aged and older Chinese adults from the CHARLS cohort, short nighttime sleep (<6 h) was associated with higher odds of psychological frailty (OR = 1.27) compared to 6-8 h of sleep, with nonlinear associations showing turning points at 7.56 h for nighttime sleep and 8.55 h for total sleep. Persistent short sleep was also associated with higher odds of psychological frailty (OR = 1.44).

papers.title: Environmental enrichment preserves intestinal endocannabinoid signaling under LPS-inflammatory conditions.
papers.summary: In adult male mice, environmental enrichment for four weeks before LPS challenge mitigated LPS-induced alterations in intestinal endocannabinoid system signaling, inflammatory mediators, barrier markers, and microbiota-derived metabolites in the proximal colon. The findings suggest that environmental context modulates endocannabinoid system regulation and may influence responsiveness to ECS-targeting pharmacological interventions.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.summary: This paper proposes VAD-EmotionNet, a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in a 3D valence-arousal-dominance space. It achieves competitive performance on the DEAP and DREAMER benchmark datasets using leave-one-trial-out cross-validation.

papers.title: Intermittent theta-burst stimulation versus sham stimulation for suicidal ideation and psychiatric symptoms in depressive disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of six randomized controlled trials compared intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) to sham for suicidal ideation and psychiatric symptoms in depressive disorders. iTBS significantly reduced suicidal ideation (SMD=-0.51), depression severity (SMD=-1.06), and anxiety severity (SMD=-0.68), but not sleep quality, with small evidence base and heterogeneity limiting certainty.

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG spectral features to explore brainwave patterns linked to left and right brain dominance in ADHD, ADHD subtypes, and control groups. The Asymmetric Index findings suggest a differential power spectrum density pattern in ADHD subjects, with higher average PSD in the right brain during working states and in the left brain during resting states, and theta and alpha waves more dominant in the left hemisphere irrespective of task state, with theta notably prominent in the frontal region.

papers.title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring.
papers.summary: An in situ gelation strategy using a fluidic precursor of gelatin and tannic acid formed conformal ionic bioelectronic interfaces on the skin, reducing skin-electrode contact impedance to 30 kΩ at 10 Hz (vs. 191 kΩ for commercial pastes) and increasing signal-to-noise ratio from 24.9 to 27.8 dB. The interface enabled electromyography-based gesture recognition with 93.4% accuracy and electroencephalography recordings of eye-state-dependent α-rhythm modulation and sleep-related waveforms.

papers.title: Association of Sleep Duration with MASLD Status and Hepatic Steatosis Index in Korean Adults: The Indirect Role of Sedentary Behavior.
papers.summary: In 26,909 Korean adults, sleeping ≤4 hours was associated with higher odds of MASLD (OR = 1.44) and ≥8 hours of sedentary time with higher odds (OR = 1.17), while mediation analysis found a statistically significant but minimal indirect effect of sedentary behavior on the sleep duration-hepatic steatosis index relationship. The authors conclude that the very small correlations offer little empirical support for a meaningful mediation pathway.

papers.title: Which Domains of Cognition in Older Adults Are Affected by Sleep Duration? A Scoping Review.
papers.journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 23 studies (2009–2024) on the relationship between sleep duration and cognitive domains in older adults. Both short and long sleep durations were associated with impairments in learning, memory, and complex attention, with gaps in research on social cognition and gender differences.

papers.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 57-year-old woman with persistent post-concussion syndrome after a motor vehicle collision, where standard neuroimaging was normal but multimodal functional testing revealed abnormalities in eight domains (vestibular, qEEG, pupillary, postural, oculomotor, cardiac autonomic, olfactory, computerized concussion). A 10-modality rehabilitation program reduced Concussion Symptom Checklist scores from 92 to 0 within 17 weeks, with near-complete resolution maintained at 10 months.

papers.title: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a critical narrative review of modern concepts and unani perspectives.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review compared classical Unani descriptions of I'yā Dhātī (spontaneous fatigue) subtypes with contemporary ME/CFS using structured searches and eight primary Unani sources. I'yā Tamaddudī showed the greatest phenomenological overlap with ME/CFS, but no clearly documented classical equivalent of delayed post-exertional malaise (PEM/PESE) was identified.

papers.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 10-year-old boy with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability who underwent genetic evaluation after unremarkable karyotyping and chromosomal microarray. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo frameshift variant c.1239_1240del, p.(Gln414Valfs*25) in ADNP, confirming Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome.

papers.title: Sleep duration and prevalent osteoporosis among U.S. postmenopausal women: a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2007-2018 with assessment of potential effect modification by physical activity.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 4,775 U.S. postmenopausal women from NHANES 2007–2018, a U-shaped association was found between sleep duration and prevalent osteoporosis, with the lowest odds at approximately 7.16 hours per night; high physical activity modified the association, with stronger odds for short and long sleep among high-activity women.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance and its associations with night shift work, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among urban operation-supporting workers: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 3,667 urban operation-supporting workers in Chongqing, China, sleep disturbance prevalence was 94.1% among healthcare workers, 85.1% among environmental sanitation workers, and 92.8% among transportation workers; night shift work and anxiety symptoms were associated with higher sleep disturbance prevalence, with anxiety showing the most stable association.

papers.title: Part 1 of a 2-part, open-label clinical trial evaluating repeated nicotinamide riboside parenteral administration: 3 consecutive days of intramuscular and subcutaneous injections
papers.summary: This open-label pilot trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of repeated daily intramuscular or subcutaneous injections of nicotinamide riboside (50 or 100 mg) for 3 consecutive days in 39 participants. Daily injections were well tolerated with no unexpected adverse events, and average daily percentage increases in whole-blood NAD+ were consistent across groups (7.83–9.97%), with exploratory benefits on fatigue and sleep.

papers.title: A scoping literature review of factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States.
papers.summary: This scoping literature review examined factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States, screening 2893 records and including 11 studies. Burnout was associated with intrinsic program factors, extrinsic factors, and individual factors; one randomized trial found a mindfulness application reduced burnout after six weeks, though longer-term effects were mixed.

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.summary: A 5-year-old boy with fever, headache, and dizziness had normal brain MRI but EEG sharp waves; CSF targeted next-generation sequencing detected Epstein-Barr virus, and symptoms resolved completely with ganciclovir and follow-up EEG normalization, highlighting that EBV-associated CNS involvement can occur with normal MRI and mild CSF abnormalities.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.summary: The study investigated how viewers process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings using eye-tracking, EEG, and semantic ratings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. AI-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-AI works, indicating broader attentional exploration and increased engagement, while professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness but differed in cultural authenticity perception.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
